summary: One native run of NAT-044 loader-diag-reset (RECOVERY a3189ca7…ea34e) under decision 0021/0019. The host alone recorded: phone left the bus at +3.6 s after the reboot request, and re-enumerated as 04e8:685d SAMSUNG USB (Download Mode) at +73.0 s without owner action (baseline of nine earlier runs: SEC_UPLOAD at about +95 s). U1+U2 supported, U3/U4 supported by the pre-registered rules. Stock RECOVERY restored in one NAT-013 session, full-hash readback equals stock, Android verified.
evidence_category: native-device: one run of a loader image on this S24 via the RECOVERY slot, observed by the host USB watcher; no register values or display frames were captured

established: After the loader ran, the phone left the bus at +3.6 s and appeared as 04e8:685d SAMSUNG USB at +73.0 s with no owner action, between the 45 s deadline and the 76 s split point to the watchdog path.
No SEC_UPLOAD was seen in the 240 s window; the device was still in Download Mode at the end of it.
The NAT-013 restore from that Download Mode state succeeded and Android returned with the stock RECOVERY (full-hash readback).
not_established: The register state at loader entry (INFORM2/INFORM3/0x190 values) and the loader's own read-back results: drawn on screen only, not captured.
The cause of the re-enumeration is inferred from timing and from Download Mode vs SEC_UPLOAD; one run, 3 s margin to the split point.
The Bootloader word 0x1234560d (loader-diag-reset-bl), anything about the USB controller, GPU or XNU execution.
findings: An unattended restore path now exists: reset into Download Mode and NAT-013 restore without the owner pressing keys.
Before this run a clk_summary read (NAT-051) restarted the phone through SEC_UPLOAD by itself; the Download Mode path in this run was not that path (product SAMSUNG USB, 04e8:685d, not SEC_UPLOAD).
